system_overview: This specification provides an abstract model of the termination detection problem in a ring of nodes with asynchronous communication. Unlike the synchronous variant, this specification accounts for messages that may be in transit (pending) between nodes. It serves as a high-level specification in a refinement hierarchy: EWD998 (Safra's algorithm) refines this specification, which in turn can be related to the synchronous termination detection specification.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring. Each node can be active or inactive and may have pending messages waiting to be received. A global termination detection flag indicates whether termination has been detected. The specification abstracts away the mechanism of detection, allowing nondeterministic detection whenever the system is terminated.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the activation status of each node (active or inactive), (2) the number of pending messages at each node (messages in transit that have not yet been received), and (3) a boolean flag indicating whether termination has been detected.
initial_state: The activation status of nodes is unconstrained (each may be active or inactive). No messages are pending initially. The termination detection flag may be false, or true if all nodes happen to start inactive with no pending messages.
actions: Four types of actions are defined: (1) Terminate: an active node becomes inactive. Termination detection may be triggered simultaneously if the system is now fully terminated. (2) Send message: an active node sends a message to another node, incrementing the receiver's pending message count. (3) Receive message: a node with pending messages receives one, becoming active and decrementing its pending count. (4) Detect termination: when all nodes are inactive and no messages are pending anywhere, the detection flag can be set to true.
safety_properties: The safe property states that if termination has been detected, then the system is actually terminated (all nodes inactive and no pending messages). A quiescence property ensures that once terminated, the system remains terminated.
liveness_properties: If the system terminates (all nodes inactive and no pending messages), then termination is eventually detected.
model_bounds: The number of nodes N is declared as a constant positive natural number. A state constraint limits the number of pending messages per node to at most 3 for model checking.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for the detect termination action. An inductive invariant combining type correctness and safety is provided for verification with the Apalache model checker. A quiescence action invariant and trace invariant are provided for alternative verification approaches.
